div.div: وُفُورٌ and ↓ وَفْرٌ and ↓ وَفْرَةٌ and ↓ فِرَةٌ [are inf. ns., (see 1,) used as simple substs.,] all signify the same: (S, TA:) Fulness, completeness, perfectness, wholeness, or entireness: (S:) or muchness, abundance, ampleness, or copiousness: (TA:) and the second also, richness; or competence. (A, K.) You say, هٰذِهِ أَرْضٌ فِى نَبْتِهَا وَفْرٌ, (S,) and ↓ وَفْرَةٌ , (S, A,) and ↓ فِرَةٌ , (S, A, K,) i. e., وُفُورٌ, (S, A, TA,) This is land in the herbage of which is fulness, &c., (S,) or abundance; (TA;) the herbage of which has not been pastured upon. (S, A, TA.) And هُوَ فِى وَفْرَةٍ مِنَ المَال [He is in possession of abundance of property]. (A.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
